origin.description: Extract the first code point that belongs to a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error.

origin.details: The match is one code point, not a merged run. No match, a missing string, or a missing pattern yields NA.
origin.example:
x <- stri_extract_first_charclass("AaBb", "\\p{Ll}")
sentence <- paste0('stri_extract_first_charclass("AaBb", "\\p{Ll}") returns ', x, '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Extract the first code point that belongs to a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error. Membership is ICU 76, Unicode 16.

translation.details: The match is one code point, not a merged run. No match, a missing string, or a missing pattern yields NA.
translation.value: A list of strings. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringi.charclass import stri_extract_first_charclass
x = stri_extract_first_charclass("AaBb", "\\p{Ll}")
sentence = f'stri_extract_first_charclass("AaBb", "\\p{{Ll}}") returns {x[0]}.'
print(sentence)
